name: 博多 一風堂 南青山店
address_ja: 〒107-0062 東京都港区南青山3-8-37 第2宮忠ビル B1 - CLOSED since 19 June 2016
cuisine: Was the Aoyama branch of Hakata Ippudo - tonkotsu ramen at the 白丸元味 / 赤丸新味 / からか麺 core, plus a branch-only 博多中華そば reviving the Edo-style soy ramen the founder sold in 1985, and a weekday 8:00-10:00 'morning ramen'; lunch ran under 1,000 yen. Closed since 2016.
neighborhood: Minami-Aoyama 3-chome, in a basement on Aoyama-dori - 3-4 min from Omotesando (Ginza / Hanzomon / Chiyoda lines) and 4-5 min from Gaienmae (Ginza line)
gf_detail: Moot - the branch is shut. For the record: Ippudo's tonkotsu is served with wheat noodles and the chain makes no gluten-free claim at any Japanese branch. Nothing here was ever workable for celiac.
vegan_detail: Moot - the branch is shut. Pork-bone broth throughout. Note for whoever re-points this record: the chain's Harajuku Takeshita-dori branch does now list 「プラントベースラーメンあり」 (a plant-based ramen) among its services on Ippudo's own store page, which the closed Aoyama branch never did.

chef_bio.origin: Fukuoka - the first Ippudo opened in Daimyo, Chuo-ku, Fukuoka City in 1985
chef_bio.background: The Minami-Aoyama branch opened on Wednesday 10 August 2011 in a basement on Aoyama-dori near the Omotesando crossing, and it was pitched as a deliberately fuller-range Ippudo: besides the standard 白丸元味, 赤丸新味 and からか麺 it carried a branch-exclusive 博多中華そば, a revival of the Edo-style soy-sauce ramen Kawahara sold at the original Daimyo shop, plus a 特製ラーメン loaded with seven toppings, 博多づけ麺 kept on as a regular rather than a summer item, and a Monday-to-Thursday 8:00-10:00 morning ramen - eight ramen in all. The opening announcement aimed it squarely at Aoyama office workers, Omotesando shoppers and local residents. It lasted just under five years: a Tabelog reviewer who visited in June 2016 photographed the closure notice on the door and recorded 19 June 2016 as the final day of business. Tabelog now carries the listing under the 【閉店】 flag with a 3.07 rating from 71 reviews. No Ippudo has replaced it in Omotesando or Aoyama; the nearest operating branches on the chain's own store locator are ハラカド店 (渋谷区神宮前6-31-21, Tokyu Plaza Harajuku 'Harakado' 5F), 原宿竹下通り店 (渋谷区神宮前1-19-9, opened 27 July 2024) and 恵比寿店 (渋谷区広尾1-3-12).
chef_bio.philosophy: Kawahara's line has always been that the shop should be 'changing constantly in order not to change' - which is why the Aoyama branch was allowed to carry a menu no other branch had.
chef_bio.specialty: 白丸元味 and 赤丸新味 tonkotsu; the branch-only 博多中華そば; weekday morning ramen from 8:00.

anecdotes.text: The opening release for 10 August 2011 said the branch's distinguishing feature was simply that it had more kinds of ramen than any other Ippudo - eight, including a Minami-Aoyama-only Hakata chuka soba reviving the 1985 original shop's soy-sauce bowl.

A reviewer who dropped in during June 2016 wrote: 'I went back to Ippudo Minami-Aoyama after a while and there was a closing notice pasted up. According to it, 19 June 2016 is the last day of business.'
Regulars used to warn each other about the entrance - the shop was down in a basement off Aoyama-dori and easy to walk straight past.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog listing 13129677, fetched with an iPhone UA (HTTP 200), carries the 【閉店】 flag, the Restaurant JSON-LD address 港区南青山3-8-37 第2宮忠ビルB1 with coordinates 35.666964/139.715049, the FAQPage hours block and the access note '東京メトロ表参道駅より徒歩4分／外苑前駅より徒歩5分'. Its review list gives the closing date from a customer who read the notice on the door. 開店閉店.com carries the 10 August 2011 opening release with the same address and phone 03-5772-8373. Ippudo's own store locator (stores.ippudo.com) was checked for every Tokyo branch and has no Omotesando or Aoyama shop.

gf_cross_contamination.text: A wheat-noodle tonkotsu shop with no gluten-free line of any kind. Academic now that it is shut.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The branch-only 博多中華そば was explicitly a soy-sauce ramen; standard wheat shoyu, no tamari claimed anywhere.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Pork-bone broth was the house product. The chain only began listing a plant-based ramen at selected branches (e.g. 原宿竹下通り店) years after this one closed.

cultural_comfort.note: Do not send anyone here. The basement unit at 南青山3-8-37 has not been an Ippudo since 19 June 2016. If the app wants an Ippudo in this part of Tokyo, the live options are ハラカド店 on the 5th floor of Tokyu Plaza Harajuku 'Harakado' at 神宮前6-31-21 (about 1.1 km north-west of this pin), 原宿竹下通り店 at 神宮前1-19-9 B1 - which is the one that lists a plant-based ramen, an English menu, card and IC payment - and 恵比寿店 at 広尾1-3-12.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION and CLOSURE. The light record read simply 「一風堂」 at 青山・表参道, which is a brand, not a shop. Exactly one Ippudo has ever stood in that neighbourhood - 博多 一風堂 南青山店, 港区南青山3-8-37 第2宮忠ビルB1, 300 m from the light record's approximate pin - and it is permanently closed, final day of business 19 June 2016 (Tabelog carries the 【閉店】 flag; the date comes from a customer who photographed the closure notice on the door that month). Ippudo's own store locator confirms there is no Omotesando or Aoyama branch today. Coordinates have been moved to the real street address because it is evidenced, but the record should be HIDDEN as permanently closed, or re-pointed by a human at ハラカド店 / 原宿竹下通り店 / 恵比寿店, which are named in cultural_comfort.

roles: operated by 丹波篠山地域活性化センター (Tanba-Sasayama regional revitalisation centre)
chef_bio.background: Kuromame no Yakata is a regional-revitalisation centre with a shop and a buffet restaurant attached, dedicated to the Tanba-Sasayama black soybean - the largest-grained kuromame in Japan. Its own site tells the local origin story, that Oda Nobunaga's rakuichi-rakuza free markets were held in the Miyata district about 800 m south of the building. The restaurant side is the 田舎バイキング, a country buffet of hand-made dishes using local produce and the black beans, 11:00-15:00 with bookings taken from 9:00; the shop runs 9:00-17:00; the centre closes Tuesdays, and Tuesdays and Wednesdays in January and February. A hand-crafts market (ささやま手創り市) runs on the 11th of every month. The site was live and posting in July 2026. None of this is in Tokyo and none of it belongs in this record.
chef_bio.philosophy: Regional revitalisation through the Tanba-Sasayama black soybean; gentle cooking that leaves the ingredients' own flavour intact.

name: 豆腐料理 空野 恵比寿 (とうふ 空野)
address_ja: 〒150-0013 東京都渋谷区恵比寿4-7-2 シーズエビス 1F
cuisine: Tofu specialist where the house tofu is set at your table from fresh soy milk and natural nigari (空野豆腐 小 1,200 yen, from two people) and the rest of the card runs through morning-cut yuba sashimi at 980 yen, avocado tofu at 500 yen, yuba gyoza, nama-fu dengaku and a table-side tempura service - lunch 1,000-1,999 yen, dinner 5,000-5,999 yen
neighborhood: Ebisu 4-chome, on the Garden Place side - 3 min from the JR Ebisu east exit (Yamanote and Saikyo lines), 6 min from Ebisu on the Tokyo Metro Hibiya line
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim of any kind, and wheat is worked hard in this kitchen - the published menu carries 生麩田楽 at 850 yen (nama-fu is pure wheat gluten), 湯葉餃子 at 880 yen (wheat wrapper), a table-side tempura service fried to order, and a crab and soy-milk cream croquette. Set against that, the thing the shop is actually famous for is naturally wheat-free: the tofu is made in front of you from Hokkaido Tokachi Toyomasari soybeans pressed to a 14-degree soy milk and set with natural nigari, with the shop's own copy stressing that no additives and no commercial coagulant go into it. The yuba sashimi and avocado tofu are likewise soy and nothing else. The exposure is in the seasoning and the fryer: the dipping sauces are ordinary wheat shoyu and ponzu unless you ask, and the same kitchen is battering tempura all evening. Workable only if you can explain yourself in Japanese and stay on the cold tofu and yuba dishes - hence 'ask', not 'options'.
vegan_detail: Not a vegan restaurant and it does not present itself as one. The card is full of animal protein - 鶏もも肉の山椒焼き, まぐろのたたき, 合鴨と生湯葉のおろしポン酢, 昆布〆サーモン, 海老しんじょう, ずわい蟹コロッケ - and the operator's own page makes a feature of 産地直送の地鶏料理, free-range aka-zasa shamo chicken sourced direct from the farmer as the 'supporting actor' to the tofu. What genuinely exists for a vegan is a handful of a la carte items: the house tofu itself, avocado tofu, the morning-cut yuba sashimi, vegetable tempura (okra, pumpkin, myoga) and the tofu desserts. Nothing is labelled vegan and the dashi behind the ponzu and the dengaku miso is not published, so assume bonito until someone asks. 'limited' rather than 'options' for that reason.

roles: operator of the とうふ 空野 group
chef_bio.origin: Kobe - FOODGATE is headquartered at 神戸市中央区磯上通6-1-9 神戸MKビル2階C
chef_bio.background: Sorano is not a one-off; it is one arm of FOODGATE, a Kobe-based restaurant company founded on 26 September 2001 when the dining business was carved out of its predecessor Cosmo-M. The company runs a small set of tightly-themed Japanese formats - ごはんや 一芯, 板蕎麦 香り家, うどん 山長, 板蕎麦 山灯香, 茶漬 分福 - and とうふ 空野 is its tofu one. The first Sorano opened in Minami-Semba, Osaka in March 2002; Shibuya and Ebisu followed in October 2002, which makes the Ebisu shop one of the two original Tokyo branches and now more than twenty years old. It was fully refurbished in July 2022. FOODGATE won the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries' 19th Excellent Food Service Industry Award in July 2011, and by the August 2025 financial year the group turned over 2,041 million yen with 89 salaried staff and 288 part-timers. The Ebisu room seats 58 including an 8-seat counter and a 10-seat terrace, is entirely non-smoking, has zashiki and horigotatsu seating, takes children, and is the sort of place Tabelog reviewers file under 'hideaway'. Lunch takes no reservations and no cards.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「添加物や凝固剤を使用しない豆腐作りを一番に考えております」 - tofu made without additives or commercial coagulant comes first, and everything else is built around it. The house line is that they are using an old ingredient to invent completely new dishes, guided by the knowledge of the people who came before.
chef_bio.specialty: 空野豆腐, set at the table from 14-degree soy milk of organic Hokkaido Tokachi Toyomasari soybeans with natural nigari (1,200 yen, minimum two people); morning-cut yuba sashimi; seasonal tofu dishes; direct-sourced aka-zasa shamo chicken; tofu desserts - tofu tiramisu 630 yen, soy-milk rare cheesecake 600 yen.

anecdotes.text: The tofu is not brought out finished. Fresh soy milk and natural nigari arrive at the table and set into tofu in front of you, and the shop's whole pitch is that you eat it at the moment it becomes tofu.
The company names its soybean: organic Toyomasari from Tokachi in Hokkaido, which it calls the summit of round-soybean cultivation, extracted to an unusually rich 14-degree soy milk.
The Ebisu and Shibuya branches both opened in October 2002, six months after the first Sorano in Minami-Semba, Osaka; Ebisu was given a full refurbishment in July 2022.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: FOODGATE's own shop page for とうふ 空野 (HTTP 200) gives the Ebisu address 〒150-0013 東京都渋谷区恵比寿4-7-2 シーズエビス1F, the phone 03-5798-7331, the walking directions from both Ebisu stations, the full opening hours and the 8/15-17 and new-year closures, plus the soybean, the no-additive tofu policy and the shamo chicken. Its 会社情報 page gives the corporate history and dates. Tabelog listing 13005528, fetched with an iPhone UA (HTTP 200), carries Restaurant JSON-LD with coordinates 35.645757 / 139.713115, the same address and phone, the 5,000-5,999 yen dinner and 1,000-1,999 yen lunch bands and a 3.48 rating from 567 reviews; its dtlmenu page carries the itemised, priced menu quoted in gf_detail and vegan_detail, the 58-seat plan, the October 2002 opening date and the no-reservations-at-lunch rule.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Tempura is fried to order and served at the table, so wheat batter is in the air and in the oil all service. A crab and soy-milk cream croquette is also on the standing menu.
生麩田楽 (850 yen) is on the standing menu. Nama-fu is pure wheat gluten - the single most dangerous item in a tofu restaurant, because it looks like a tofu dish.
湯葉餃子 (880 yen) uses a wheat gyoza wrapper despite the yuba name.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No gluten-free tamari is claimed anywhere by the shop or the operator; assume ordinary wheat shoyu in every dipping sauce, and wheat-based ponzu on the aigamo and yuba dishes.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The operator's own page makes direct-sourced aka-zasa shamo chicken a headline feature alongside the tofu, and the menu carries tuna, duck, kombu-cured salmon, prawn and snow crab. The dashi behind the ponzu and the dengaku miso is not published.

positives.text: The house tofu is made on the premises from named organic Hokkaido Tokachi Toyomasari soybeans with natural nigari and, by the company's own stated policy, no additives and no commercial coagulant - so the headline dish is soy and water, with nothing hidden in it.
Several dishes are naturally free of both wheat and animal products before seasoning: the house tofu, avocado tofu (500 yen), morning-cut yuba sashimi (980 yen) and the vegetable tempura items.

cultural_comfort.note: An easy room to walk into - three minutes from the JR Ebisu east exit, 58 seats, entirely non-smoking, children welcome, cards and PayPay accepted at dinner, and a picture-heavy menu with 1,947 photographs on Tabelog if you would rather point. Two practical catches: lunch takes no reservations and no credit cards, so bring cash between 11:30 and 14:30; and dinner is a 5,000-6,000 yen a-la-carte evening rather than a set course, so it adds up. If you need the wheat-free route you will have to explain it in Japanese - the staff are used to explaining the tofu, not to allergen handling, and 生麩 sitting on the menu next to the tofu dishes is exactly the trap a non-Japanese-reading celiac would fall into. Booking by phone on 03-5798-7331; the shop posts on Instagram as @sorano.ebisu.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「そら野 カフェ」 at 恵比寿駅東口, described as 植物ベース・カフェ. There is no cafe by that name. An Ebisu-scoped Tabelog keyword search for そら野 (/tokyo/A1303/A130302/rstLst/?vs=1&sk=そら野, HTTP 200) returns exactly one business: 豆腐料理 空野 恵比寿 - same reading, Sorano - at 渋谷区恵比寿4-7-2 シーズエビス1F, which Tabelog and the operator both place 3 minutes from the JR Ebisu EAST exit, matching the light record's own neighbourhood string, and 330 m from its approximate pin. The identification is solid; two of the light record's other fields are not. It is not a cafe - it is a tofu-cuisine restaurant and dining bar open 11:30-14:30 and 17:00-23:00 - and it is not plant-based: the operator features direct-sourced shamo chicken and the menu is full of tuna, duck, salmon, prawn and crab. Name, coordinates, address, hours, website, cuisine, gf and vegan tiers have all been rewritten from the shop's own site (foodgate.net/shop/sorano/) and its Tabelog listing and priced menu page. The nationwide check was run too: Tabelog's national index for そら野 returns そら野テラス and そら野デリカ in Niigata and the sister branch 豆腐料理 空野 渋谷, none of which fits Ebisu. Gnavi returned zero for そら野 恵比寿, which is why the kanji-spelling route mattered.
